newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Meridor holds talks on 1997 budget.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Meridor holds talks on 1997 budget.

text.p: Israeli Finance Minister Dan Meridor spent Wednesday in talks with ministers and legislators seeking support for the 1997 budget and a second round of cuts he will bring to the cabinet next week.
Treasury sources said there was a good chance Meridor would announce the exact size of the proposed second round of budget cuts on Thursday.
The additional cuts, expected to be as much as 2.3 billion shekels, are due to be given to the cabinet for approval next Monday.
Meridor met legislators from parties within the government coalition that is led by his Likud party.

The treasury's 1997 budget, which originally called for 4.9 billion shekels in spending cuts, faces strong opposition in parliament even from within Likud on grounds the cuts will fall hardest on the disadvantaged.

Meridor is determined to keep next year's deficit to 2.8 percent of gross domestic product. This year's deficit may swell to as much as four percent, Meridor said on Tuesday, compared with a 2.5 percent target.
